analysis: Documentation-only PR: docs/developer/test.md (date bump plus a new ModelCheckpointRestoreContentionLiveTests section, head lines 177-203) and docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md (date bump plus a new 'Provider-staged destinations' row at about line 119 describing zeroed host-byte staging that avoids MLX evalLock). No source or code changes are in the supplied units, so no security controls are changed by the diff itself. The new test doc advises running the live test with `env -i` and only listed variables, with an isolated ephemeral cache and spec. It states never to use production cache roots or keys (test.md line 163 is retained). No new attack surface or credential handling appears. The ssd-kv-cache row asserts a behavior change in the provider-staged import path. The zero source is read by the copy and can briefly commit up to one destination (<=64 MiB) outside the MLX allocator. This touches TB-007 and the encrypted prefix-cache threat T-041 (cross-tenant cache sharing/TTFT oracle) and memory-accounting/admission. The doc claims this is bounded. The underlying code (CheckpointHostZeros.swift, CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift, PagedCheckpointStorage.swift, CompleteCheckpointImportPlan.swift) was not supplied, so the security effect cannot be verified. Possible concerns for later passes: whether the unaccounted host commit can be abused for memory pressure/DoS (the ledger charge), whether zero-initialized staging prevents residual-data leakage across tenants (T-028), and whether restore-vs-cold TTFT contention changes the timing-oracle posture in T-041. The test also measures restore TTFT under another tenant's prefill. The unit 0c2e5345ee82eaef:0 is metadata only (no text). The TB-011 and TB-002 definitions are unaffected by these edits.
